title: Shard and seat request signing sends a 13-digit millisecond timestamp even where uutils date prints nanoseconds for %3N
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run the command in `run.cmd` (bash, openssl on the PATH). One test puts a fake `date` that behaves like uutils (`%3N` prints nine digits of nanoseconds) first on the PATH and runs deploy/scripts/shard-sign.sh without --timestamp.
S2: Read the result of each test named in `run.tests`.
expect: Every test named in run.tests reports ok.
x-shard-timestamp has exactly 13 digits and is within 60 s of the test's clock.
fence: No server, no network: the signer runs locally against a fake date; host-dsh-init.sh is read as text.

tests: with no --timestamp the signer uses 13-digit milliseconds, even under uutils date
step 6 signs with seconds x 1000, never date +%s%3N (uutils prints nanoseconds: 403 stale)
a POST signed in bash passes tracy-host verifyHostCall (the same string when the method is POST)
